name: Barbell Snatch
summary: An Olympic weightlifting movement where a barbell is lifted from the floor to overhead in one continuous, explosive motion.

setup: Stand over the loaded barbell with feet hip-width apart and the bar over the balls of the feet.
Grip the bar with a wide snatch grip using a hook grip, keeping arms long and relaxed.
Lower the hips, lift the chest, pull the shoulders slightly ahead of the bar, and flatten the spine to build full-body tension.
steps: Initiate the first pull by pushing through the full foot to elevate the bar smoothly past the knees while maintaining the back angle.
Once the bar clears the knees, transition into the second pull by violently extending the hips, knees, and ankles while bringing the bar close to the hip crease.
Shrug the shoulders and pull the body downward rapidly under the rising bar.
Turn over the wrists and punch aggressively against the bar into a full overhead squat with arms locked.
Stabilize the bottom position, then stand erect to full hip and knee extension with the barbell locked overhead.
Lower or drop the barbell forward under control onto a lifting surface.
instructions.breathing: Take a deep breath and brace the core tightly before initiating the pull from the floor; exhale forcefully once standing fully erect at the completion of the lift.
cues: Punch up fast into the catch

common_faults.fault: Swinging the barbell outward away from the body in an arc.
common_faults.correction: Keep the lats engaged and elbows high and outside during the pull to keep the bar traveling vertically close to the torso.

common_faults.fault: Bending the arms prematurely before complete hip extension.
common_faults.correction: Keep arms long like ropes until the hips and knees reach full extension in the second pull.

common_faults.fault: Catching with soft elbows and pressing out the bar overhead.
common_faults.correction: Pull under the bar aggressively and punch into a crisp, immediate lockout before catching the load.

precautions: Use bumper plates on a designated lifting platform with ample clearance.
Practice dumping and bailing the barbell forward and backward safely before handling heavy loads.
